messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — Acme (Alex) is stuck on the POC. Streaming completions keep failing when they go through their corporate proxy. They can hit the hosted API fine from a laptop but their app behind the proxy gets repeated timeouts. Can SEs triage?

alex_cust: Repro steps: node service uses our TS SDK, streaming with response.on('data'). Works locally. In their environment we see socket hangups after ~30s. No consistent HTTP status in our logs (sometimes 502 from their proxy, sometimes connection reset).

josh_se: Thanks, Alex. Can you paste a minimal request and any error stack you see? Also which SDK version?

alex_cust: Using @redwood/inference 0.12.1. Minimal snippet:

```
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'open-lite', messages });
stream.on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d));
```

Error on their side: "Error: socket hang up" and sometimes "ECONNRESET" in node logs.

josh_se: Sounds like proxy is closing idle connections or buffering chunked responses. Two quick checks: 1) can they run curl -v --no-buffer to the streaming endpoint from the same host? 2) confirm env vars HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY being set and whether the proxy rewrites responses.

alex_cust: Running curl -v --no-buffer https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream returns a 502 after ~28s. Verbose shows the proxy sending a 502 upstream prematurely.

lina_pm: Alex — are you using any SDK-level retry or timeout configs? Might be masking the root.

alex_cust: We set axios timeout to 60000ms. The hangups occur before that.

josh_se: For Node SDK, important: the underlying http.Agent keepAlive and maxSockets matter. Some corporate proxies tear down connections if you open many short-lived sockets. Try configuring the agent in client options: 

```
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 10 });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ agent });
```

Also try setting `signal` or explicit request timeout separate from axios global.

alex_cust: Will try. Any changes needed server-side for streaming to handle proxies?

josh_se: Proxies often buffer responses before sending to client; NGiNX for example can buffer chunked responses and will return 502/504 if upstream takes too long. If they control the proxy, ask for "proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_set_header Connection \"\";". If they don't control it, workaround is to fall back to non-streaming (polling) or increase proxy timeouts.

tim_oncall: Also check if their proxy inspects TLS (MITM) and closes long-lived streams. If corporate appliance rewrites TLS it can kill streaming. Suggest they try an outbound rule to allow direct egress to api.redwood.ai for the POC host to validate.

alex_cust: Confirmed proxy is a BlueCoat cluster. They said it buffers responses and enforces a 30s idle limit. We can request a rule but timeline is slow.

lina_pm: Can we suggest SDK fallback behavior for POC? E.g., automatic chunk-aggregation and final response polling if streaming is interrupted.

josh_se: For short-term, implement an app-level rehydration: detect ECONNRESET/socket hangup during stream and re-issue a non-streaming completion call with same prompt + token to resume. For TypeScript: collect partial tokens and on reconnect pass prefix to model with stop tokens. Not ideal but workable for demo.

alex_cust: Ok we'll implement fallback. Any headers we can send so proxy treats it as normal JSON?

josh_se: You can try adding `Connection: close` to force each request to be independent, but that loses keepAlive. Alternatively, set `Content-Type: text/event-stream`? Our streaming uses chunked transfer; proxies vary in behavior.

deploy_bot: [deploy] redwood/inference-sdk@0.12.2 released with small networking docs update (no code changes).

tim_oncall: On the Python side, note: requests default doesn't stream nicely. Use httpx with `timeout=(5, None)` and `stream=True` to keep reading. Example for clients using python: 

```
async with client.stream("POST", url, json=payload, timeout=(10, None)) as r:
  async for chunk in r.aiter_bytes():
    process(chunk)
```

And ensure trust_env True if behind proxy to pick up env vars.

alex_cust: Quick question on rate limits: if we fallback to polling multiple times will we hit token-based throttles? They're on a trial account.

josh_se: Good call — polling increases request count. Check headers `x-rate-limit-remaining` in responses. For POC we can temporarily bump their quotas; I'll coordinate with sales.

maria_sales: Yes, I can authorize a 2x request quota bump for the trial window. I'll update the POC sheet and let the customer know. :thumbsup:

alex_cust: Thanks everyone — implementing fallback + node agent changes now. I'll update after we validate.

josh_se: If they still see 502 after agent + fallback, capture tcpdump and full curl -v output and we can escalate with network team.

alex_cust: Quick update: agent keepAlive reduced 502 frequency. Fallback works for demo flow. We'll follow up on proxy exception with IT for production. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
